title: My God, How Many Are My Fears
description: My God, How Many Are My Fears in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 3, part 1, headed “Doubts and fears supprest; or, God our defence from sin and Satan”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, how man-y are my fears! How fast my foes in-crease! Con-spir-ing my e-ter-nal death, They break my pre-sent peace.

lines: My God, how many are my fears!
And all my swelling sins appear
But thou, my glory and my strength,
Shalt silence all my threatening guilt,
I cry'd, and from his holy hill
I call'd my Father, and my God,
He shed soft slumbers on mine eyes,
In spite of all my foes;
I woke, and wonder'd at the grace
What though the hosts of death and hell
Terrors no more shall shake my soul,
Arise, O Lord, fulfil thy grace,
My God has broke the serpent's teeth,
And death has lost his sting.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
